literal: Close friends' faults even, spreading, those of the habit - what indeed strangers towards?
translation: If people have the habit of broadcasting even the faults of their close friends, what will they do to strangers?
modern: நெருங்கிய நண்பர்களின் குற்றங்களையே ஊரறியத் தூற்றும் பழக்கம் உடையவர்கள், முன்பின் தெரியாத அயலாரிடம் என்னதான் செய்வார்களோ?
explanation: This couplet highlights the destructive and untrustworthy nature of those who habitually backbite. The word 'துன்னியார்' refers to close, intimate friends, while 'ஏதிலார்' means strangers or outsiders. The poet asks a rhetorical question: if someone is willing to expose and spread ('தூற்றும்') even the flaws of their closest companions, what limits would they have when dealing with strangers? It warns that a slanderer spares no one.
